speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) from 2011 to 2021, what is the annual number of cases of mental distress or psychiatric issues reported by teaching staff in (i) Primary schools, Secondary schools and Junior Colleges, (ii) Institutes of Technical Education, (iii) Polytechnics, and (iv) Autonomous Universities; and (b) in light of the next normal of living with COVID-19 and home-based learning in 2020/2021 and beyond, what is the Ministry doing to alleviate the stress encountered by teaching staff.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, whether there has been an increase in a teacher’s workload and blurring of lines between work and personal time; (b) whether steps have been taken to measure the mental health index of our teachers; and (c) whether there are efforts to ensure that our teachers are not overwhelmed and suffer from burnout.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Our teaching staff have shouldered a heavy responsibility to ensure that our students can continue learning safely during this COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Workload for teaching staff has increased as they are responsible for ensuring that students are educated about and comply with the safe management measures.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Each time a confirmed case is notified, staff need to follow-up on contact tracing and communications.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: When home-based learning (HBL) was declared, teaching staff also needed to make the necessary arrangements, with additional support for students who may not adjust as well to HBL.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: All these efforts are necessary to allow teaching and learning to continue, despite the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: To keep track of staff sentiments and well-being, the Ministry of Education (MOE) conducts dipstick polls, school visits by senior management and engagement surveys.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) also conduct surveys and staff engagements with leaders.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: MOE and the IHLs have put in place measures to address the concerns raised by staff on workload.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: At the system-level, MOE has reprioritised initiatives and reduced schools’ involvement in HQ work and pilots.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Schools have also been given greater flexibility to pace the implementation of selected initiatives, including deferring implementation, if it helps to spread out staff workload.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: At the school-level, we recognise that ground practices may vary.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We have called on school leaders to reprioritise school programmes, establish clear expectations on teachers’ availability and work hours and encourage supervisors to check in with their officers regularly.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For example, school leaders have been providing guidance on avoiding parent-staff communications after school operating hours except for urgent matters, such as those involving the safety and well-being of students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This can minimise the blurring of lines between work and personal time.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In line with the streamlined health protocols, ring-fencing policies and contact tracing processes in schools have now also been significantly simplified and teachers’ workload related to COVID-19 management is being reduced.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Similarly, the IHLs have implemented various measures tailored to their institutions, such as reprioritisation of work tasks, to reduce workload and setting clearer expectations that staff need not reply to work emails after office hours unless there are exigencies.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: To support staff who need help, MOE provides free counselling services.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In addition, MOE, Polytechnic and ITE staff who are public officers can access the whole-of-Government counselling hotline.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Staff in the Autonomous Universities have access to either in-house or external counselling services.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Similarly, the number of IHL teaching staff seeking counselling support has increased.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We do not have more detailed data, as information from all counselling sessions is kept confidential and staff are not required to report mental distress or psychiatric issues.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We recognise the exceptional demands that COVID-19 has placed on our staff and have put in additional effort to promote a positive and supportive work environment for staff well-being across schools and IHLs, such as organising workshops covering stress management and self-care.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: To support staff in implementing home-based learning effectively, MOE and the IHLs have provided professional development courses and resources.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Learning teams within and across schools also allow staff to collaborate and share good practices on the design and delivery of online lessons.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The well-being of our staff is of paramount importance and MOE and the IHLs will continue to strengthen our support for staff to help ensure their well-being.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I have three supplementary questions for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I should say a couple of things to set the context as I answer the three supplementary questions from Mr Patrick Tay.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: First, I think we should all thank our teachers and educators because, over the last two years, it has really been very tough on them.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We are one of the few systems in the entire world that have managed to keep our schools going and to allow our students to continue learning with minimum disruptions during the last two years.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, I really want to say a big "Thank You" to all our teachers for going all out.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In order for us to switch seamlessly from physical schooling to home-based learning, our teachers need to spend a lot of time preparing more than two sets of lesson plans: one set of lesson plans for the school, the physical schooling; and one set of lesson plans for the home-based learning, just in case we need to switch over seamlessly.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On top of that, to be able to take care of the higher-needs students who would still need to return to the school during the home-based learning period.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On top of all this, the school leaders and teachers also have to perform the role of contact tracing in case there are cases in the school.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We have to do this without additional manpower support.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We have seen the challenges that even MOH, together with the support of the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF), had and how big a challenge this can be.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, all the more, I am deeply appreciative of the efforts by our teachers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Over the course of the last two years, be it the vaccination programme or the mental and social emotional stresses experienced by our students and their families, many of these will culminate in their experiences in the school, which our teachers also have to manage.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: With that at the back of our mind, what can we do as a society to help our teachers manage?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Because they are, ultimately, not only teachers but they are also fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They also have families that they need to take care of.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The fundamental belief is this: if our teachers are well taken care of, they will be able to take care of all our children well.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But if our teachers are not well taken care of, if they are not in the best condition, then it is also very difficult for us to expect them to take good care of our children, our students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In the short term, as I have mentioned, we have adjusted various programmes in order to lighten the workload of our teachers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We have adjusted the schedule as to how we roll out new programmes.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The second thing that we can do in the short term is to use technology for us to scale up the lessons, especially for home-based learning.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: While in the long term, this will help to lighten the workload of our teachers, in the short term, it actually requires our teachers to do more because we have to switch over from the current physical schooling curriculum to the online curriculum.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Many of our teachers will need to learn new skills.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But our hope is that, over the longer term, as we leverage technology to scale up the lesson preparation and even some of the class sizes, then we will be able to devote more time to the higher-needs students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Overall, as a system, it is quite unrealistic for us to expect that we can double the amount of resources overnight.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In order to focus more attention and bandwidth on the high-needs students, we will need to find other ways to scale up our curriculum teaching so that we can save some time and bandwidth on the other areas where we can.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: An example of this is, this year, Term 4, where we took one extra day to declare it as a school holiday after the PSLE marking.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That one extra day would have given us a period of about nine days continuously for some of our teachers to take a bit of a break and to spread out their load during the PSLE marking.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: These are things that we will continue to do.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We try not to make too many changes too quickly.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This allows time for the teachers and the school leadership teams to make the necessary adjustments.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In the longer term, we would need to do much more to help our teachers cope.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: One is to use technology to scale up our teaching resources so that we can, as I have mentioned, apply the time more surgically to the higher-needs students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The second thing that we can do to better equip our teachers to manage this is to equip them with the skillsets to detect potential mental health issues among the students and their fellow peers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We are applying it, starting from the National Institute of Education (NIE) curriculum, all the way to their professional development and continuing training.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, these are things we will do over the longer term.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Over the longer term, I would also like to see our teachers systematically given a break or sabbatical, whereby they can go out and recharge themselves.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I do not think our teachers are afraid to work hard.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But in working hard, they must be given a sense of agency, that they are in control, that they are doing things with conviction.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And this is why I keep emphasising that no matter how hard our teachers and school leaders work, they must feel that they are in control, with a sense of agency.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They can take charge of things, they can customise the curriculum according to the needs of their students, because every school has a different profile of students and no two children are similar.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We need to allow teachers and school leaders that autonomy to customise the programmes according to their school needs, according to their students' needs.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The second thing that I think I would say is that we, as a whole-of-society, must also help our teachers in a form of partnership.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Our teachers care a lot, many of our teachers even give their handphone numbers to their students, just in case their students get into trouble outside school hours.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And I have heard many stories of our students, sometimes calling the teachers in the middle of the night because they got kicked out of home, because of family issues and our teachers respond.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is the extent to which our teachers go, to take care of our students beyond the curriculum time in school.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But in giving out their handphone numbers to the families and the students, we also hope that the families will not abuse the trust.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is one thing for the child to call up the teacher at midnight to say that he is in trouble.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is another thing for the parent to call up the teacher at midnight to ask whether tomorrow the child has spelling and should wear a red or blue T-shirt.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If the child does not remember, so be it.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We, as parents, do not need to overly protect our children and deprive them of the learning experience.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I think we need to establish this clear understanding as expectations of parents and society, and that of ourselves, get heightened, a lot of expectations are projected onto our teachers as well.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Last but not least, I would say this: in the COVID-19 situation, there are many changes.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We may not be perfect and we will not be perfect.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: All of us can pull together and help one another overcome some of the imperfections that we are facing.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Sometimes, we have to make changes at the last minute because of the circumstances.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But all of us can pull together and help one another.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For example, some families prefer HBL, some families prefer physical schooling.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: There will not be a situation where we can meet the needs of everyone.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But we can all help one another, that when we do not get the things that we want for ourselves, for our families, let us not burden the teachers with the excessive demands on the teachers to try and fulfil our own personal needs.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That, I think, will go a long way in helping our teachers cope as well.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is perhaps unfair for the teachers if they are unable to spend their time and take care of all the students because of the high demands placed on them by a very small group of parents.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: If I can remind Members, perhaps let us confine our supplementary questions to just two.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And if I can request our office holders to keep the responses short.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: And I thank Minister Chan for sharing about the short- and long-term perspectives of supporting teachers.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I think our Government has always been very good with adopting technology enablement to support all our civil and public servants.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: We have always done very good on that front.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: But Minister Chan has also acknowledged that a lot of the stress that the teachers feel come from students reaching out to them, things that happen outside of the classroom.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: So, I would like to add on to the perspective of our support to teachers on the human support element.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: When we try to support someone, but we also require them to go through further training to provide peer support, again it adds to the load on their bandwidth and stress.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: And lastly, the question is about whether MOE is effecting any kind of mindset change within the system and amongst school leadership and principals to change their mindset towards the notion that hard work is what it is, and teachers just need to suck it up.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Because I think we have seen interviews of teachers that they feel like they do not have a safe space to go to.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: So, thank you, I hope the Minister can clarify on this.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: First, on the issue of training, we do want to equip our teachers to pick up the signs of distress that may happen to their students and also to their fellow peers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: To the extent that we can, we would want to do this as part of their professional training.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Having said that, one of the things about counselling services is this: be it students or teachers, they all need someone that they can trust in order for them to open up to the counsellors or to the peer, to share.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Without this trusting relationship, it is not a function of how many counsellors that we have.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Even if we have the counsellors, be they para-counsellors or full-time counsellors, we need this trust relationship to be established.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Which is why from Secondary schools and above, we try as much as possible for the first layer to have the peer support, for each of them to be able to identify their own issues and also to look out for their peers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And then, we escalate it to either the family or the teachers, and we escalate it next level to the full-time counsellors.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As I have mentioned in my reply, there are services available to all our teachers as part of the Public Service as well.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Definitely, we want to promote a safe environment for people to come forward and seek help.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Which is why, just now, in my reply, I mentioned that we do not actively go and track the number of people who seek help because we do not want to give people the wrong impression, that if people seek help, they become a part of the statistics and so forth.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We tend to look at mental health as a black or white issue: I am mentally okay, or I am mentally not okay.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Let us look at it as a kind of fitness level.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We all grow in our fitness level, with a bit of training.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Today, I might not be able to run as fast or as far.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But with a bit of training, tomorrow I can run further and faster.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Today, I might not be able to cope with some things.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But tomorrow, with a bit of training, stretching, I might be able to cope a bit more and that is how we grow as individuals.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If we move away from the binary concept of mental health, then I think it would encourage people to come forward and say that we are much more prepared to come forward and seek help, if we think that we are unable to accomplish a task.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Once we overcome that level of fitness and we become even fitter, we can then take on more stresses and that is how we grow as a person.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: With that perspective and that mindset in all school leaders, teachers and students, we will be able to better encourage our people to seek help when they need to.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And it is just to stretch ourselves a bit more, to train ourselves up so that we can do better tomorrow than what we have done today.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I seem to recall that I had mentioned that it should be only two supplementary questions.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: To keep it simple for Members, can we just have one supplementary question per person?
